resolutions.researcher_notes: Searched Russian first. cdu.ru (TEK Russia / CDU energy-statistics agency, RU) explicitly names this pipeline among Tajik Transgaz's currently-held balance of trunk gas pipelines: 'На балансе «Таджиктрансгаза» находятся: магистральные газопроводы... в том числе газопроводы «Келиф — Душанбе»...' (Tajik Transgaz holds on its balance the trunk gas pipelines... including the Kelif-Dushanbe gas pipeline) -- this lists it as active current infrastructure, not a decommissioned/historical asset. This is the same page the sheet already cites; re-verified live (200, token present) -- the DEAD_LINK classification on the input brief appears to be an automated-check false negative from searching the literal English string 'operating' on a Russian-language page (matches the deep-sweep audit's finding on this row). Corroborating, independent, English-language: Times of Central Asia (2026-08-26, 'Turkmenistan Gas Exports: Could Tajikistan Become a New Market?') confirms Tajikistan's 2024 gas imports (~267 million cubic meters) were Uzbek-origin gas moving through the existing corridor, i.e. gas is currently flowing to Dushanbe over this trunk system -- supports the pipeline's physical asset being in current operating use. CAVEAT (carried from the deep-sweep audit, not grounds for a status change): the same article frames any TURKMEN-origin gas reaching Tajikistan via Kelif as still prospective/on-paper as of Aug 2026, so the Turkmen segment specifically may be idle while the Uzbek segment is what is actively moving gas -- flagged for whoever next reviews FuelSource/segment-level flow, not a Status concern on this operating trunk.

The only source that names StartYear1=1975 for this specific pipeline is the UN Statistics Division PPT (unstats.un.org/unsD/energy/meetings/cis2011/ac.240-p2_fuel.ppt), reachable only via a web.archive.org capture. Re-tried today: direct curl to both the brief's cited capture (20260812163236) and the earliest known capture per the archive.org availability API (20220722114946, confirmed to exist via https://archive.org/wayback/available, which itself IS reachable) both timed out; WebFetch also reported it is unable to fetch from web.archive.org. This matches the country note's documented network condition (archive.org's API answers, web.archive.org content-serving does not, on this machine) -- not evidence the capture is bad, but per the access-failure rule I cannot cite a page I could not actually read this session. Searched in Russian for an independent alternative naming a 1975 start year for the Kelif-Dushanbe line specifically: cdu.ru (already used for Status) names the pipeline but gives no build/commissioning year, only an aggregate current network length; ria.ru's 2003 wire on Turkmen-Uzbek pipeline-transfer talks names the pipeline but is dated 2003 with no construction-year content. Russian Wikipedia pages (Kelif, Economy of the Tajik SSR) do state a 1975 build year, corroborating the sheet's value, but per source_roster.md Wikipedia is never citable directly and was read for leads only. Found no citable non-Wikipedia independent source for 1975. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than citing an unreadable capture or a banned source.

Same access problem as Start [ref]: LengthKnown=300.00 km is sourced only to the unstats.un.org PPT via a web.archive.org capture, and web.archive.org content-serving was unreachable from this machine today (confirmed by direct curl timeouts on two different capture timestamps, including the earliest one on record per archive.org's availability API, plus a WebFetch refusal) -- a network condition, not a dead-link finding, so per the access-failure rule I am not citing a page I could not read. Searched in Russian for an independent length figure for this specific line: cdu.ru gives only an aggregate figure (917 km total across five named Tajik trunk lines, not broken out per line) and neither ria.ru nor the other seed citations state a per-line length. Separately worth flagging (per the deep-sweep audit, outside this ref-sweep's scope to resolve): the row's own mapped RouteAccuracy=high geometry yields LengthEstimateKm=406.14 km, 35% longer than the 300 km 'known' figure -- a genuine spec discrepancy that a route-integrity review should look at, not something this pass can adjudicate. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than citing an unreadable capture.

Two independent Russian sources both name the pipeline using exactly its two endpoint place names, which is what supports StartLocation=Kelif / EndLocation=Dushanbe: cdu.ru lists 'газопроводы «Келиф — Душанбе»' among Tajik Transgaz's held trunk pipelines (i.e. the Dushanbe end sits on Tajikistan's own operated network, consistent with EndCountryOrArea=Tajikistan -- Dushanbe is Tajikistan's capital, an uncontested fact). ria.ru (2003) independently names 'Келиф-Душанбе' as one of two trunk TRANSIT gas pipeline sections (with Мубарек-Келиф, i.e. Mubarek-Kelif) under Turkmen-Uzbek intergovernmental negotiation to transfer sections TO Turkmenistan -- consistent with Kelif being the Turkmenistan-side origin/border point of the corridor (Kelif is a settlement in Lebap Province, Turkmenistan, on the Amu Darya), matching StartCountryOrArea=Turkmenistan. Neither source states 'Turkmenistan'/'Tajikistan' as bare country labels for this line -- that attribution rests on standard, uncontested geography (Dushanbe = the capital of Tajikistan; Kelif = a Turkmen town) rather than being independently re-derived from a gazetteer this session: geonames.org's Kelif entry (geonameId 1219017) is JS-rendered and returned no country text to url_verifier despite a 200, so per rule 3 it was not cited. Tier kept at medium (place-name identity confirmed by 2 independent sources; country attribution not independently re-sourced).

Reused and re-verified the deep-sweep audit's fill finding on this exact unit (row's audit shard, fills[0]) rather than re-deriving from scratch -- concur with its conclusion after an independent re-check today. cdu.ru confirms Tajik Transgaz as the balance-holder/operator of this pipeline on Tajik territory -- only ONE of the three named operators (Узтрансгаз, Tajik Transgaz, Turkmengaz). On cdu.ru, Uztransgaz appears only as Tajikistan's gas SUPPLIER (import contract context), not as pipeline operator. Re-checked mfa.gov.tm/en/articles/84 (Turkmenistan's list of its own main export gas pipelines) today: it does not mention Kelif, Kelif-Dushanbe, or Tajikistan among its named pipelines at all, confirming the audit's finding that this URL is irrelevant to this specific line despite being a live 200. Found nothing independently naming Turkmengaz as operator of a Turkmen segment of this specific line. Leaving UNRESOLVED per the country's calibration: a genuine Russian-language search that comes up short on a state-monopoly multi-country asset is an honest UNRESOLVED, not a failure to look.

Owner1/2/3 = Uztransgaz, Tajik Transgaz, Turkmengaz -- the same three-party claim as Operator [ref], and it fails to clear the bar for the same reason. Of the three current_ref URLs: utg.uz/ru/about/history/ re-verified today as a confirmed HTTP 404 (via url_verifier and a raw curl status check), so it cannot support anything and should be dropped as dead, not kept as an inaccessible-but-live page. mfa.gov.tm/en/articles/84 is live (200) but re-read in full today -- it is Turkmenistan's own enumerated list of its main EXPORT gas pipelines (Turkmenistan-China, Dowletabat-Deryalyk, Korpeje-Kurtkui, Dowletabat-Hangeran, East-West) and Kelif-Dushanbe is not among them; it does not mention this pipeline at all, so it is a live but irrelevant citation for this Owner claim. cdu.ru (the third current_ref, live) names Tajik Transgaz as the balance-holder of this pipeline within Tajikistan -- independent support for Owner2=Tajik Transgaz only, not for the primary_value Uztransgaz or for Turkmengaz. Tried the utg.uz Wayback capture (20260314231446, confirmed to exist per the availability API) as a possible replacement for the dead utg.uz page, per the dead-link protocol -- web.archive.org content-serving was unreachable from this machine today (same network condition as the Start/Length units), so it could not be read or cited. No independent source found naming Uztransgaz or Turkmengaz as co-owners of this specific multi-country line (as opposed to being each country's national gas company in general). Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than citing a 404, an irrelevant-but-live page, or an unreadable capture.
